Query Databricks SQL as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__databricks.R
oauth_db_databricks.Rd

Query a Databricks SQL warehouse with DBI or dbplyr through brickster. Users can sign in with Databricks OAuth or Microsoft Entra.

Usage

oauth_db_databricks(
  authorization,
  host,
  warehouse_id = NULL,
  ...,
  http_path = NULL,
  auth_mode = c("databricks_oauth", "entra"),
  target = if (auth_mode[[1L]] == "entra") "databricks" else NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

host

Databricks workspace hostname or HTTPS origin.

warehouse_id

SQL warehouse ID. Supply this or http_path.

...

brickster connection options, such as catalog and schema.

http_path

Warehouse HTTP path, such as "/sql/1.0/warehouses/warehouse-id". Supply this or warehouse_id.

auth_mode

"databricks_oauth", or "entra" for Azure Databricks with Microsoft sign-in.

target

Token target name. Defaults to "databricks" for Entra. Databricks OAuth uses the authorization's default token.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning a brickster DBI connection.

Details

Install brickster. Create con inside server() and get connection <- con() in a render or reactive expression before querying.

For other brickster functions, use oauth_db_databricks_api().

Connection lifetime

The helper replaces the connection when its stored token changes. A saved connection can retain its token after local sign-out; call con() for each operation.

See also

oauth_db_databricks_client(), oauth_db_databricks_api(). vignette("databricks", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Other database connections: oauth_db_azure_postgres(), oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_fabric_sql(), oauth_db_hana(), oauth_db_oracle(), oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_redshift(), oauth_db_snowflake(), oauth_db_sql_server(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_trino()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_databricks(
  auth$connection,
  host = "example.cloud.databricks.com",
  warehouse_id = "warehouse-id"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user()")
})
} # }
